title: A nervous Dassault is spending $2bn on AI, in the division dragging it down
excerpt: Dassault Systèmes is one of Europe’s largest software companies, and it is having an anxious year. Its shares are down about a quarter this year. It pushed out its chairman in February. And investors worry that a new wave of AI could hollow out its main business. Its answer, announced on Thursday: spend up to […]
content_html:
Dassault Systèmes is one of Europe’s largest software companies, and it is having an anxious year. Its shares are down about a quarter this year. It pushed out its chairman in February. And investors worry that a new wave of AI could hollow out its main business.

Its answer, announced on Thursday: spend up to $2 billion on a company most people have never heard of.

The French firm has agreed to buy ArisGlobal, a maker of drug-safety and regulatory software. The price is roughly $1.8 billion in cash, plus up to $200 million more tied to future AI revenue. The seller is Nordic Capital, a Swedish private-equity group that has owned it since 2019. The whole sum comes from Dassault’s own cash pile.

What Dassault is buying

ArisGlobal is not a household name, but it sits deep inside the pharmaceutical industry. Founded in 1989, it is based in Waltham, Massachusetts. It serves more than 200 customers, including half of the world’s 50 biggest drugmakers, plus biotechs and government health regulators. Its software processes more than 12 million patient safety reports a year. It expects revenue of about $175 million in 2026.

Its appeal to Dassault is the AI inside it. ArisGlobal’s NavaX system uses generative AI for the grind of drug-safety monitoring and regulatory filing. Those tasks are heavily manual, and heavily policed. The company says it cuts that work by more than 30%. The market for such compliance software could reach $7.5 billion by 2030.

Dassault is not alone in shopping. Legacy software firms, from SAP to Adobe, have bought their way into AI rather than build it from scratch.

The virtual-twin bet

Dassault’s speciality is the “virtual twin,” a detailed digital copy of a real machine, factory or, increasingly, a human body. It uses these to help 390,000 customers design cars, planes and drugs. Chief executive Pascal Daloz wants to fuse that with ArisGlobal’s real-world patient data. The goal, he says, is the industry’s first platform to “unify real-world evidence with virtual evidence.”

“Life Sciences is entering a new era of innovation, driven by AI and the shift to precision medicine,” Daloz said.

ArisGlobal’s chief executive Aman Wasan put it more bluntly. “The future of Life Sciences will not be built on better software. It will be built on connected intelligence.”

A deal born of pressure

The optimism sits on top of real strain. Dassault has spent 2026 among the software firms investors fear AI will upend. The specific threat is “world models,” which let machines grasp the physical world without a hand-built twin. The stock fell hard. The chairman left abruptly in February. This is Dassault’s first big deal since.

Awkwardly, the division it is doubling down on is its weakest. Life-sciences revenue fell 4% in the second quarter and 12% in the first, dragging on results, Bloomberg reported. Its last big health bet, the 2019 purchase of clinical-trials firm Medidata, has underwhelmed. Now it is betting on the same sector again. The wager: that AI turns the laggard into the growth engine.

Investors, for now, approved. Dassault shares rose about 5% on Thursday. It also reported solid quarterly results, with revenue up 4% and cloud growing 14%. The deal should close in the second half of 2026, subject to regulatory approval. Whether it can also quiet the deeper fear, that AI is coming for the twin-makers too, is the harder question.

content_html_zh:
达索系统是欧洲最大的软件公司之一，今年是令人焦虑的一年。 今年其股价下跌了约四分之一。 该公司于二月份罢免了董事长。 投资者担心新一波的人工智能浪潮可能会掏空其主要业务。

周四公布的答案是：斥资 20 亿美元收购一家大多数人从未听说过的公司。

这家法国公司已同意收购药品安全和监管软件制造商 ArisGlobal。 价格约为 18 亿美元现金，再加上与未来人工智能收入相关的高达 2 亿美元。 卖家是 Nordic Capital，一家瑞典私募股权集团，自 2019 年以来一直拥有该物业。 全部资金来自达索自己的现金储备。

达索正在购买什么

ArisGlobal 并不是一个家喻户晓的名字，但它在制药行业中占有很深的地位。 该公司成立于 1989 年，总部位于马萨诸塞州沃尔瑟姆。 它为 200 多家客户提供服务，其中包括全球 50 家最大制药商中的一半，以及生物技术公司和政府卫生监管机构。 其软件每年处理超过 1200 万份患者安全报告。 预计 2026 年收入约为 1.75 亿美元。

欧盟科技的💜

来自欧盟科技界的最新传言、我们明智的创始人鲍里斯的故事，以及一些值得怀疑的人工智能艺术。 每周都会免费发送到您的收件箱中。 立即注册！

它对达索的吸引力在于其内部的人工智能。 ArisGlobal 的 NavaX 系统使用生成式人工智能来进行药物安全监控和监管备案。 这些任务都是大量的手动任务，并且受到严格监管。 该公司表示，该工作量减少了 30% 以上。 到 2030 年，此类合规软件的市场规模可能达到 75 亿美元。

达索并不是唯一一家进行购物的公司。 从 SAP 到 Adob​​e，传统软件公司已经通过收购进入人工智能领域，而不是从头开始构建人工智能。

虚拟双胞胎赌注

达索的专长是“虚拟双胞胎”，即真实机器、工厂或越来越多的人体的详细数字复制品。 它利用这些帮助 390,000 名客户设计汽车、飞机和药品。 首席执行官 Pascal Daloz 希望将其与 ArisGlobal 的真实患者数据融合起来。 他说，目标是成为业界第一个“将现实世界证据与虚拟证据统一起来”的平台。

“在人工智能和向精准医疗转变的推动下，生命科学正在进入一个创新的新时代，”达洛兹说。

ArisGlobal首席执行官Aman Wasan说得更直白。 “生命科学的未来不会建立在更好的软件之上。 它将建立在互联智能的基础上。”

迫于压力而达成的交易

乐观情绪是建立在真正的压力之上的。 2026 年，达索一直是投资者担心人工智能会颠覆的软件公司之一。 具体的威胁是“世界模型”，它可以让机器在没有手工构建的双胞胎的情况下掌握物理世界。 该股大幅下跌。 董事长二月份突然离职。 这是达索自此以来的第一笔大交易。

尴尬的是，它正在加倍投资的部门是其最薄弱的部门。 据彭博社报道，生命科学业务第二季度收入下降 4%，第一季度下降 12%，拖累业绩。 2019 年收购临床试验公司 Medidata 是该公司最后一次重大健康押注，但效果并不理想。 现在它再次押注于同一领域。 赌注：人工智能将落后者变成增长引擎。

目前投资者已经批准了。 达索股价周四上涨约 5%。 它还公布了稳健的季度业绩，收入增长 4%，云计算增长 14%。 该交易预计将于 2026 年下半年完成，尚需获得监管部门批准。 更难的问题是，它是否也能平息更深层次的恐惧，即人工智能也将降临到这对双胞胎制造者身上。
